# Fun With Science

> Rigorous, data-first critiques of fringe scientific and pseudoscientific claims. Every assertion checked against published data.

## Projects

- [Dome Model Review](https://funwithscience.net/dome-model-review/): A scientific critical review of the "Ovoid Cavity Cosmological Model" (ECM) — a flat-earth dome cosmology that claims 69 confirmed predictions. Every claim is evaluated against published data and against the model's own internal consistency.
  - Detailed LLM index: https://funwithscience.net/dome-model-review/llms.txt
  - Sitemap: https://funwithscience.net/dome-model-review/sitemap.xml

- [Kell Solar Measurement Analysis](https://funwithscience.net/kells-analysis/): A measurement-by-measurement check of Corey Kell's "Operation Resolute Time" (ORT 2020, Kabul) and "Operation North American Sun" (ONAS 21-23, Fayetteville) solar-elevation datasets — a flat-earth "45° limit" claim tested against standard globe-model solar geometry across 133 readings.

- [Globe Deconstruction](https://funwithscience.net/globe-deconstruction/): A claim-by-claim review of Levi Miller's prerelease book "Globe Deconstruction?" and the three claims at shapedebate.com — twenty-four checkable claims graded as stated, each page conceding what is right, re-deriving every number from public data, and ending with tests that could go against it. In progress: 18 of 24 answered.

- [Inside the Flat Earth App](https://funwithscience.net/flat-earth-pro-analysis/): A code-level look at the "Flat Earth" mobile app (free Android build, November 2026). Its sky view places stars with the standard equatorial-to-horizontal transform using observer latitude; its flat map shades day and night with per-point solar altitude on a sphere and is one of several projections of the same longitude/latitude data. Includes short code excerpts and globe-vs-literal-map predictions. In progress: screen-recorded tests pending.

## Tools

- [Reverse Refraction Solver](https://funwithscience.net/refraction-solver/): A curvature calculator inverted — from observer height, distance, target height, and observed visible height it solves the implied refraction coefficient and required temperature gradient on a globe and on a flat plane, with uncertainty propagation and reference regime bands (normal marine, minor/major looming, duct/Fata Morgana).
- [Two Disks, One Sky](https://funwithscience.net/star-trails/): Interactive star-trail simulator for the flat-earth two-disk dome model — reproduces the outside-camera counter-rotation trick, shows the overlap that grows with disk radius, and renders a virtual Tenerife panorama (28.3° N) beside a real long-exposure photograph for comparison against a single-axis globe sky.
- [Does Gas Need a Container?](https://funwithscience.net/gas-containment/): Interactive gas containment simulator for the flat-earth claim that the atmosphere needs a dome — a particle model in real units that sets gas pressure against gravity in four cases: the bromine-into-vacuum two-bulb demo (with a second-law entropy ledger), a sealed tank from 50 cm to 100 km, a heavy gas in an open tank, and an open column of air with and without walls, a dome, or gravity, compared with the 1976 US Standard Atmosphere and a radiosonde sounding.

## About

funwithscience.net publishes rigorous, reproducible critiques of fringe scientific claims. The data behind each analysis is publicly available and the scripts that compute it are published alongside the pages. The intent is to separate genuinely predictive claims from post-hoc relabels of already-established physics, and to do so in a way an independent reviewer can audit end-to-end.
